jobs.description:
In order to fill a fixed-term position in full-time (39.83 hours/week = 100%) at the earliest possible date, we are looking for 1

Full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of decentralized security

Join a World-Class Research Team in Information Security The Chair for Information Security at Ruhr University Bochum — led by Prof. Dr. Ghassan Karame and part of the Faculty of Computer Science since 2021 — brings together an international, multicultural team of researchers pushing the boundaries of decentralized and systems security. Our work spans a broad spectrum of security and privacy challenges, with a particular emphasis on decentralized security and distributed machine learning security. We are proud to be affiliated with: • Horst Görtz Institute for IT Security (HGI), one of Europe's most respected centers for fundamental research in computer security. Founded over two decades ago, HGI maintains deep collaborations with world-renowned academic institutions, industry leaders, and media partners — and has been a launchpad for numerous successful cybersecurity startups. CASA — Cluster of Excellence: Securing the Digital Society is a leading center for cybersecurity research at Ruhr University Bochum. Through an innovative and interdisciplinary research program, CASA strengthens the resilience of the digital society, bringing together internationally renowned researchers to develop next-generation security solutions that holistically protect large-scale socio-technical systems, spanning cryptography, hardware and software, and the intersection of technology with users and society. Funded by the German Research Foundation (DFG) with €53 million for its second phase from 2026 to 2032, CASA is hosted at the Horst Görtz Institute (HGI) at RUB and partnered with the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy (MPI-SP).

The Chair for Information Security has an immediate full-time PhD position (m,f,x) in the area of (decentralized) systems security (currently 39.83 hours /week = 100%).

Scope: full-time
Duration: fixed-term, 3 Jahre
Start: at the earliest possible date
Apply by:  2026-11-02

Your tasks:

- The main task in this position is to research, analyze, and improve the security and privacy of modern decentralized platforms while enhancing their performance and scalability.
- Members of Prof. Karame's Chair conduct research and teaching in various areas of IT security. The Chair offers various courses in the Bachelor's and Master’s degree programs and participates in several third-party-funded projects.
- This international and dynamic team also cooperates with several university and non-university institutions (e.g., the Max Planck Institute for Security and Privacy).

Your profile:

- Bachelor’s or Master’s degree in Computer Science or related field
- Excellent interpersonal and communication skills in English
- Background in the areas of IT security and privacy, system security, and distributed systems is a plus.
- Experience in software development including experience with programming languages, such as Python, Golang, Java, or C/C++ is also a plus.

responsible UFZ units. Coordinate the transition from project

support. We offer The freedom to master even the most demanding

The Department of Pediatric Oncology, Hematology and Clinical Immunology at the University Hospital Düsseldorf (UKD) at the Heinrich Heine University (HHU), headed by Prof. Dr. Arndt Borkhardt, is one of the leading clinical centers for the diagnosis and treatment of childhood cancer in Germany. The clinic is part of the University Tumor Center (UTZ) at the UKD and the Center for Integrative Oncology Aachen-Bonn-Cologne-Düsseldorf (CIO-ABCD), which is funded by the German Cancer Aid. It is a founding partner of the German Consortium for Translational Cancer Research (DKTK) Essen-Düsseldorf and participates in international research consortia and study groups. The clinic operates a fully equipped research laboratory (safety level 1 and 2 according to the Genetic Engineering/Biotechnology Ordinance, including a GMP, next generation sequencing, flow cytometry, life cell imaging, and high-throughput drug testing facility) with 5 research groups and >30 staff working in an interdisciplinary manner on the fundamentals of childhood cancer and in the field of therapy optimization. We are seeking a highly motivated and creative PhD Student to join our research program in the field of amino acid homeostasis and cancer metabolism, with an anticipated start date of 02/2027. The successful candidate will work on the ERC-funded project “POWERFUL” (Deciphering how cancer cells fuel themselves to advance personalized treatment strategies).
The PhD student will take a leading role in understanding how cancer cells sense and respond to amino acid availability, and how to translate this knowledge into precision-based treatment strategies. This position requires scientific independence and the opportunity to contribute intellectually to experimental design, data interpretation, and publication strategy. The candidate will employ and further develop advanced experimental models and methodologies, including organoid systems, patient-derived xenografts (PDXs), CRISPR/Cas9-based genome editing, multiparameter flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, FRET assays, protein interaction and signaling assays, as well as in vitro and in vivo drug screening approaches.
Candidates should have a very good understanding of and experience with standard molecular biology techniques including but not limited to tissue culture, genome editing, FACS analysis, confocal microscopy, immunoblot, and PCR/qPCR. Experience with animal models is a plus (as is FELASA B certification). Willingness to learn and work with murine experimental models is a fundamental requirement. - Master in natural sciences or related field

- Solid experience with cancer models (e.g. organoids, PDXs) and drug-response studies
- expertise in molecular and cellular biology techniques, including mammalian tissue culture, genome editing, FACS/flow cytometry, confocal microscopy, immunoblotting, and PCR/qPCR.
- Excellent capability to develop new aspects and projects within the given research focus
- Excellent written and spoken English language skills, German language skills are a plus
- Organizational and project management experience
- Willingness to cooperate and ability to work in a team

The German Diabetes Center (DDZ) is the Leibniz Institute for Diabetes Research at Heinrich Heine University Düsseldorf. The DDZ is an interdisciplinary research center linking molecular and cell biological basic with clinical and epidemiological research approaches. The DDZ has the aim to develop new approaches for prevention, early detection and diagnosis of diabetes mellitus and to improve therapy and treatment of its complications.
The Institute for Clinical Diabetology (Director: Prof. Dr. Michael Roden) is looking for an

Epidemiologist (postdoc - m/f/d) We are searching for a candidate with (1) a doctoral degree in epidemiology, (bio)statistics or a comparable discipline, (2) the ability to work in an interdisciplinary manner with physicians and life scientists, and (3) knowledge of epidemiological methodology and statistical analysis systems (e.g. SAS or R).
